jobs.title: Senior Principal Engineer (Lead Engineer)
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Senior Principal Engineer / Lead Engineer to serve as a senior technical leader and subject matter expert for leading electrical engineering activities on large and complex industrial and power generation projects.

This role provides technical oversight, client engagement, project leadership, mentoring of engineering staff, and contributes to business development initiatives while ensuring the delivery of high-quality engineering solutions that meet project objectives, industry standards, and client expectations.

The job responsibilities for the position will include but are not limited to:

• Extensive experience with 34.5KV and 15KV Medium Voltage and Low Voltage power distribution systems, Electrical system studies (load flow, short circuit, protective device coordination, arc flash)
• Understanding of ETAP, SKM, Easypower, or equivalent software, Substation and switchgear design, and Motor control centers (MCCs), VFDs, and large motor applications
• Knowledge in Emergency and standby power systems, Area classification and hazardous location design, Grounding, lightning protection, and cathodic protection interface considerations, and Electrical specifications, datasheets, and procurement support
• Strong understanding of NEC, NFPA 70E, NESC, IEEE Standards, API, ISA, PIP, and industrial facility standards
• Serve as Lead Electrical Engineer on large and complex projects.
• Plan, schedule, and monitor discipline work.
• Manage budget, scope, and project deliverables.
• Review and approve design packages produced by junior engineers.
• Interface directly with clients, vendors, and construction teams.
• Lead design reviews, E-HAZOPs, and project meetings.
• Participate in proposal preparation and scope development.
• Support business development activities and client relationship management.
• Identify opportunities for additional work with existing clients.
• Assist in developing strategic growth initiatives for the I&G business.
• Mentor and develop junior and mid-level engineers.
• Perform technical reviews and quality checks.
• Assist with recruiting and interviewing candidates.
• Support resource planning and workforce development initiatives.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

• BA/BS in Electrical Engineering + 8 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Professional Engineer (PE) license
• Relevant industry experience in industrial, power generation, oil & gas, chemicals, LNG, terminals, or heavy industrial facilities
• Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary engineering projects

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• Masters Degree in Electrical Engineering
• 15 years of professional experience in Oil and Gas, Power Gen, or heavy industrial projects
• HV Experience on voltage levels up to 138KV
• Multiple state PE registrations
• Experience with EPC projects
• SCADA and Power Management System integration
• Field experience including commissioning and startup support
• Existing relationships with major industrial clients and equipment suppliers

• Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
• Relocation is not available for this position.

jobs.title: Chief Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

The Chief Engineer at Movenpick Resort Petra Jordan is responsible for the overall supervision, management, and leadership of the engineering department. This role ensures the smooth operation of all hotel facilities, including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems. The Chief Engineer plays a crucial role in maintaining the hotel’s safety standards, managing energy efficiency, and providing a high level of service to both internal and external guests.

Key Responsibilities:

• Leadership and Team Management:Lead and supervise the engineering team, including recruiting, training, and developing staff to maintain a highly skilled and motivated team.Assign tasks, manage shifts, and oversee daily operations of the engineering department.Provide technical expertise and support for maintenance staff.
• Maintenance and Operations:Oversee all maintenance programs, preventive maintenance, and repairs for all hotel equipment, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and fire safety systems.Ensure that all hotel facilities and systems are functioning efficiently and in compliance with safety and regulatory standards.Manage day-to-day operational issues, ensuring quick and efficient problem resolution to minimize downtime and guest inconvenience.
• Budget and Financial Management:Prepare and manage the department's budget, including controlling costs related to maintenance, energy consumption, and capital expenditures.Ensure proper inventory control of parts and supplies, as well as efficient energy and water management to optimize operational expenses.Monitor and analyze energy consumption, looking for cost-saving opportunities.
• Health, Safety, and Compliance:Ensure all building systems comply with health and safety regulations, including fire safety systems, emergency lighting, and building security.Oversee regular safety inspections and ensure compliance with all local, national, and international standards and regulations.Act as the key contact during emergencies and ensure the safety of guests and employees.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Composite Production
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.




ROLE OVERVIEW

We're looking for a Senior Manager, Composite Production to own the full composite production organization: the engineering, maintenance, and production teams that together turn composite process into finished parts at rate. You'll lead through a management layer of shift leads and supervisors - standing up standard work and quality control that survive shift-to-shift, building a maintenance program that keeps cure and layup equipment running, and growing and training the workforce as we scale - and help take composite production from prototype builds to predictable, production-ready output, in tight partnership with Advanced Engineering.

If you're energized by building a production organization from the ground up, developing people at scale, and hands-on manufacturing leadership, you'll be in the right place - and we'd be thrilled to have you on the team!




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Composite Production Performance End to End: Hold single-point accountability across engineering, maintenance, and production for quality, yield, equipment uptime, and throughput — so the three functions operate as one, unified system.

 - Lead Through a Management Layer: Build and develop the shift leads and supervisors who run the floor day-to-day, and grow that leadership structure so the organization scales without diluting quality.

 - Systematize Engineered Fixes into Standard Work: Turn one-off process solutions into trained, auditable standards that every technician on every shift can run — and close the loop back to engineering when a standard isn't holding.

 - Own Equipment Reliability: Run a preventive maintenance program and uptime tracking for cure, layup, and trim equipment (autoclaves, ovens, presses, trim and cure systems), and prioritize maintenance and engineering resources against production schedule risk.

 - Build the Workforce and Its Training Pipeline: Stand up structured training paths and certification levels - for example a station-based dojo model and skills matrices - that take a hire from no experience to certified, independent operator.

 - Run Quality Control at Scale: Put control plans, SPC checks, and non-conformance and corrective-action processes into daily practice across shifts, so quality and process control scale with production rate.

 - Partner with Advanced Engineering: Work continuously with the Advanced Engineering team to validate process robustness before it reaches the floor, treating each build as a shared outcome rather than a handoff at the end of engineering's work.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Composite Manufacturing & Organizational Leadership: Extensive experience in composite manufacturing, including leading a multi-disciplinary organization spanning manufacturing engineering, maintenance, and/or production at meaningful scale.

 - Leadership Through Leads and Supervisors: You've run production through a layer of leadership rather than by directly managing every individual, and you know how to build that layer.

 - Equipment Uptime & Maintenance Strategy: Demonstrated experience running maintenance and reliability for composite process equipment — autoclaves, ovens, presses, trim and cure systems.

 - Scaling a Workforce Through a Ramp: You've stood up or grown a production workforce — hiring, org design, and skills development — as volume increased.

 - Turning Fixes into Sustained Standard Work: You can point to an engineered process fix you converted into standardized, trained, sustained production work across a large team.

 - Hands-On Composite Production Depth: Enough working knowledge of prepreg and wet layup, vacuum bagging, cure, trim, and bonding to direct engineers and audit floor execution — paired with process discipline and variability reduction across a multi-shift workforce.

 - Quality & Production Systems Fluency: Comfort running control plans, SPC, and corrective-action processes at scale, and familiarity with MES / MBOM / routing structures and how floor, maintenance, and engineering data roll up into production metrics.

 - Bonus: Having led a composite production organization through a prototype-to-rate ramp in aerospace, marine, or automotive; built or scaled a maintenance program for composite process equipment; worked with automation (ATL / AFP / FPL, robotic trim, CNC) and how it changes staffing and training at rate; or built a dojo-style training curriculum that took entry-level hires to certified operators.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You treat process robustness as a shared outcome with Advanced Engineering and the integration team — something built together, not inherited once engineering is done. You're credible with engineers and floor leadership alike, and you hold a technical conversation and a shift-performance conversation with equal weight.

 - Creative Problem Solver: Your default reaction to a good fix isn't "problem solved" — it's "how do we make sure every shift and every technician can run this." You build durable systems where craft knowledge used to live.

 - Adaptable & Agile: You're comfortable operating in ambiguity while still building auditable systems, and you can prioritize and sequence finite resources — headcount, equipment, training — across competing needs.

 - Innovative Mindset: You're genuinely motivated by developing people at scale — building leads and supervisors who can each run a piece of a large production organization — and by designing the structure that lets quality scale with rate.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation including a robust equity incentive plan.

 - Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance - we cover 100% of your premiums.

 - 401(k) with company matching, so you can plan for the future.

 - Generous flexible time off, paid parental leave, and company-wide holiday breaks.

 - Relocation packages available for those moving to join our team.

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

Equal Opportunity Employer

REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Office Manager (Part-time)
jobs.description:

We provide the technology platform and behind-the-scenes support that lets brokers build custom insurance solutions for specific industries or customer groups. We handle the complex (technology, compliance, and partnerships with highly-rated insurance carriers), so they can focus on serving their customers and growing their business.

Authentic is looking for a part-time Office Manager to keep our Dayton office running smoothly. This role is the go-to person for everything office-related — facilities, supplies, vendors, and day-to-day logistics — working closely with People Operations, and also extending that same support to employees and visitors.

This is a great fit for someone who's organized, self-directed, and enjoys being the person who makes an office feel well cared for, without needing a lot of oversight to get there.

• Monitor inventory and restock snacks, beverages, kitchen items, toiletries, and general office supplies

Facilities & vendor management

• Coordinate approved office services and projects as needed

• Track quotes, invoices, delivery dates, installation schedules, and outstanding vendor follow-ups

Escalate sensitive, urgent, or higher-cost decisions to People Operations Associate.

Required Skills and Experience

• 1+ years of experience in office management, facilities, administrative, or hospitality roles preferred

• Reliable and consistent — someone the team can count on to show up and follow through

• Proactive and comfortable working independently, managing multiple priorities with minimal oversight

• Comfortable being on your feet and moving often throughout the day (restocking, setup/cleanup, light lifting, walking the office)

• Strong organizational skills and high attention to detail

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office/Google Workspace and general office technology

• Based in or near Dayton, Ohio, and able to be onsite during scheduled office hours

Preferred

• Experience coordinating vendors or tracking budgets, quotes, and invoices

• Experience planning office events, off-sites, or employee-recognition activities

• Experience coordinating with People/HR or property management/facilities teams

• Insurance or financial services industry experience is a plus, though not required

Position Details

Part-time, 20–25 hours per week, onsite in our Dayton, Ohio office.

Our (FTE) benefits

• Competitive salary, equity, and role trajectory

• Comprehensive health benefits for you and your family

• 401(k) plan with company match

• Unlimited PTO

• Paid parental leave

About Authentic

Authentic builds the infrastructure that program insurance runs on. We partner with leading brokerages to design and manage custom insurance programs, backed by A and A- rated carriers operating nationwide. Brokers bring the data and distribution. We bring everything else: the technology, the capacity, and the underwriting expertise to stand up specialized programs at speed and build them to last.  We’re a Series A company backed by top investors, including FirstMark Capital, Zigg Capital, Slow Ventures, Clocktower, Commerce Ventures, and Altai. We’ve grown over 15x in the past year with a massive market opportunity ahead.

Authentic is committed to building an inclusive working environment regardless of gender, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, race, education, age, or other personal characteristics. We believe that people do their best work when they can be themselves, and different perspectives and experiences make us stronger as a team. We’re proud of the supportive and inclusive workplace we're building together and are always working to make it even better.

Mantis grew from Adrian’s vision to restore and rewild degraded farmland which he developed into a widely-acclaimed Private Game Reserve. This was the first private game reserve in the Eastern Cape and the beginning of eco-tourism in a poverty-stricken province that had few opportunities outside of commercial farming. Adrian and the Mantis team successfully created a place where man and nature could co-exist sustainably. From this initial success, the Mantis model was then developed worldwide, understanding that consumers could use the Mantis portfolio as a mark of quality, consistency and character. jobs.title: Delivery Driver
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

Do you know why Domino's Pizza hires so many drivers? Well, aside from the fact that our delicious pizza is the perfect solution for dinner for families all across the nation - we do it because we can. What do we mean by that, you ask? We mean that we offer a great flexible schedule that offers the hours you're looking for. That means you're free when you need to be. You'll have plenty of time left over for school, to hang with your friends, or whatever. Even if you need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

Right now Domino's is looking for qualified drivers to staff stores in your area. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24- 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

Ready to join the Domino's delivery squad? Here's what we're looking for:

• **Age & License**: You've got to be at least 18 years old and rock a valid driver's license with a clean driving record that meets our standards. Safety first – always!
• **Your Ride**: You'll need access to an insured vehicle that's ready to roll and deliver delicious pizza to our hungry customers.
• **Navigation Ninja Skills**: Got solid map-reading abilities? Can you locate addresses like a pro and navigate through all kinds of terrain – from quiet neighborhoods to multi-story buildings? Perfect!
• **Schedule Flexibility**: You're ready to bring the heat on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, with bonus opportunities to pick up shifts during the week if you want extra cash in your pocket!
• **The Vibe**: You're reliable, punctual, and genuinely excited about getting hot pizza to people faster than anyone else. Plus, you can handle the hustle and bustle of a fast-paced environment with a smile!

At Domino's, we are a brand of honesty, transparency and accountability and we want exceptional people like you to join our team! We have continued to prove we “Put our People First” by making sure our work environment is safe and provides stability for you as a team member. The brand continues to deliver the “Power of Possible” to local Domino’s store owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores!

jobs.title: Clinic Area Lead, Florida
jobs.description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.



Overview

As the Area Director you will be accountable for bringing Neko Health’s operating model, culture, and member‑first standards to life across a growing portfolio of clinics in Florida.

This role sits at the intersection of leadership, execution, and local adaptation — ensuring that global ways of working translate into consistently high‑quality experiences on the ground, while continuing to mature and evolve as we scale.

Neko Health has now entered the US market starting with New York with a clear operating philosophy, emerging global processes, clinical standards, and service principles already in place ready to scale across the US. While these are still being built and refined, the role is firmly focused on adoption rather than reinvention — shaping how these ways of working show up locally, strengthening them through practical execution, and enabling teams to operate with increasing confidence, consistency, and care.

Reporting to the Country Leader, US, you will own regional performance end‑to‑end — from pre‑opening readiness through sustained multi‑site operations. You will act as the cultural and operational anchor for Neko Health in Florida, setting expectations, building capability, and establishing how clinics lead, operate, and serve members from day one.

 

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

 

Bring the operating model to life

 

 - Embed Neko Health’s operating model across the Florida clinics, focusing on strong leadership behaviours, cultural norms, and consistent execution rather than net-new process design. Ensure global standard are understood, embraced and brought to life in day-to-day clinic operations

 - Lead the successful local adoption of existing playbooks and standards, tailoring them thoughtfully to local regulations, team dynamics, and member expectations while preserving the integrity of Neko’s global member experience.

 - Create strong clinic‑level leadership capability by coaching managers and clinical leads on how to translate standards into practice — setting clear expectations, reinforcing accountability, and role‑modelling a member‑first mindset.

 - Operationalise readiness for new clinic openings by ensuring teams are culturally aligned, well‑trained, and confident in executing established processes, with clear ownership of go‑live success and early performance.

 - Establish clear performance rhythms (metrics, reviews, feedback loops) that reinforce behaviours, surface issues early, and continuously improve both team effectiveness and the member experience.

 - Partner closely with the Country Leader, US and central teams to ensure the global operating model works in practice locally — identifying where light adaptation is required and driving disciplined, high‑quality implementation at scale.

 
 

Clinic & Member Experience

 - Ensure each clinic consistently delivers a seamless, premium member experience aligned with Neko Health's service standards and brand promise.

 - Lead regional initiatives to elevate service quality based on member feedback, NPS insights, and frontline observations, iterating playbooks in real time as you learn.

 - Foster a hospitality-driven culture where empathy, professionalism, and precision define every member interaction — and where that culture is embedded through training, not just expectation.

 - Oversee the physical and experiential standards of all clinics — ensuring consistency in ambiance, cleanliness, and overall presentation across a growing portfolio.

 

Medical Quality & Compliance

 - Partner with Lead Doctors to build and uphold Neko's clinical quality standards in the US context — ensuring adherence to federal and state regulatory requirements from the ground up.

 - Drive continuous improvement in medical delivery and inspection readiness across all sites, establishing audit-ready documentation and escalation protocols.

 - Serve as the bridge between clinic operations and the Medical Excellence team, ensuring best practices are embedded regionally through structured processes rather than informal norms.

 - Mentor and develop Lead Doctors and Clinic Leads, building their leadership capabilities and accountability for quality outcomes.

 

Operational & Financial Performance

 - Own regional operational KPIs and full P&L accountability — building the financial frameworks alongside the clinics themselves, not inheriting them.

 - Design scalable operational frameworks, cost controls, and workflow efficiencies that can flex as the New York portfolio grows from four clinics to more.

 - Oversee workforce planning and staffing models in collaboration with central teams — building hiring profiles, ramp plans, and scheduling logic suited to New York's demand patterns.

 - Contribute to regional business strategy, including market expansion planning, new clinic launches, and network optimisation — as someone who has been in the room from the start.

 

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

 - Recruit, onboard, lead, and coach a team of Clinic Leads and Lead Physicians across all assigned clinics — many of whom you will hire yourself.

 - Build a strong culture of accountability, communication, and collaboration across distributed teams from day one, establishing the norms and rituals that will define how the Florida team works.

 - Act as the primary regional liaison between clinic teams and central functions — including Customer Support, Facilities, Workforce Planning, People Operations, Talent Acquisition, and Demand Planning.

 - Champion cross-functional alignment to ensure smooth execution and a unified member and employee experience, acting as the voice of Florida into the broader organisation.

 

Minimum Qualifications

 - Proven experience in a senior operational leadership role (Area Director, Regional Director, District Leader, General Manager or equivalent) within a premium, consumer‑facing, multi‑site environment such as premium healthcare‑adjacent, wellness, fitness or technology‑enabled services with physical operations/stores.

 - Ability to be based and/or local travel distance to Miami as this role will be based onsite. 

 - Demonstrated success implementing and embedding established operating models, standards, and playbooks across multiple locations — driving adoption through leadership, coaching, and accountability rather than documentation alone.

 - Strong track record leading clinic‑level or site‑level leaders, with the ability to build capability, reinforce culture, and translate standards into consistent day‑to‑day execution.

 - Experience operating in regulated environments, with accountability for quality, compliance, and inspection readiness, ideally in partnership with medical or clinical leadership.

 - Proven financial and operational acumen, including ownership of regional KPIs, budgets, and P&L performance in a scaling context.

 - Ability to balance strategic perspective with hands‑on execution, particularly during periods of growth, new site openings, and organisational change.

 - Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with confidence operating in a matrixed, fast‑moving organisation across central and regional teams.

 - Comfort leading through ambiguity and change, with a bias toward action, continuous improvement, and disciplined execution.

jobs.description:
Shift Manager Position

We are currently looking for an Assistant Store Manager to assist our General Manager with day-to-day operations.  We are looking for a self-motivated, organized, and hardworking individual who wishes to grow with our company and have fun while doing it.  We are a local franchise that employs 350+ people so team building skills are a must for this position.

We Offer:

• Closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas
• Flexible Schedules
• Part Time or Full Time
• Hourly Pay/Bi-Weekly Pay
• Bonuses for meeting store goals for eligible managers

Incentives Offered:

• Earned Bonuses
• Earned Paid Vacation
• Overtime
• Employee Discounts

Requirements:

• Reliable Transportation
• Food Handlers Licenses preferred
• Must be able to work days, nights, weekends, and holidays
• Must be able to work 30-50 hours per week
• Excellent Communication skills
• Organization skills
• Team Building skills
• Basic Computer skills (Word and Excel preferred)
• Basic Math and Book Keeping skills
• Must be able to Deliver and create outstanding product

Physical Requirements:

• Must be able to stand for long periods of time
• Must be able to lift up to 50lbs
• Bend and Reach
• Push and Pull
• Squat, Climb, and Balance
• Handle Extreme Temperatures (Oven, Cooler, and Outdoor Conditions)
• Repetitive use of hands
• Work with chemical cleaners (de-greaser, mop solution, sanitizer, etc.)

Education/Experience Requirements:

• High School Diploma or Equivalent preferred
• Minimum of 2 years in food industry preferred
• Minimum of 2 years of management skills preferred
• A minimum age of 18 years

Driving Requirements:

• A minimum age of 18 years
• Maximum of 3 traffic violations in 3 years or 2 in 2 years
• Reliable Transportation
• Vehicle must comply with all Store and Corporate Safety Standards
• Minimum 2 years of driving experience required
• Must have approved Vehicle Insurance that covers Delivery Drivers
• Must be able to provide MVR (Motor Vehicle Report) from DMV
• Car must have a positive image

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

· For short distances for short durations

· Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

· During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

· Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

· During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

· Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

· Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

· Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

· Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

· Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.title: Delivery Driver(7194 - Cheney)
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

Do you know why Domino's Pizza hires so many drivers? Well, aside from the fact that our delicious pizza is the perfect solution for dinner for families all across the nation - we do it because we can. What do we mean by that, you ask? We mean that we offer a great flexible schedule that offers the hours you're looking for. That means you're free when you need to be. You'll have plenty of time left over for school, to hang with your friends, or whatever. Even if you need a second job for some extra cash, Domino's Pizza is the perfect place for you.

Right now Domino's is looking for qualified drivers to staff stores in your area. We're growing so fast it's hard to keep up, and that means Domino's has lots of ways for you to grow (if that's what you want), perhaps to management, perhaps beyond. Whether it's your hobby, main-gig, or supplemental job, apply online. We're bound to have just the thing for you.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. You should possess navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area and must be able to navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings.

.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24- 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

If there are any errors in the wages posted, or in the benefits that we provide, please email docs@pacpiepizza.com with the subject WAGE TRANSPARENCY and the store location you are applying for, and we will correct the advertisement within 5 days.

Must be 18 or older with 2+ years of licensed driving experience

Must be able to provide a clean driving abstract

Must have valid Vehicle Insurance

Must have a reliable vehicle either registered in your name or able to provide a release of use to deliver in the vehicle

Must be able to perform basic adding and subtracting with monetary values

Must be able to listen to and complete basic prep tasks and cleaning assignments from management

At Domino's, we are a brand of honesty, transparency and accountability and we want exceptional people like you to join our team! We have continued to prove we “Put our People First” by making sure our work environment is safe and provides stability for you as a team member. The brand continues to deliver the “Power of Possible” to local Domino’s store owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores!

jobs.description:
This is an in office role that is responsible for providing customers, retail personnel, and insurance companies detailed information regarding invoices and explanations of balance due.

What Would You Do? The Specifics.

• Answers calls from customers regarding collection of past account accounts. Conducts conference calls with customers and insurance companies to determine the the responsible party for the balance and offers solutions of payment options.
• Provides detailed notes in our Point of System to communicate findings to retail associates and maintains notes in the ticketing system to track calls and the purpose of calls.
• Answers calls from retail personnel to assist with selecting the correct plans in the Point of Sale system and answer questions regarding plan calculations and why their customers received balance due notices.

• Answers calls from third-party payers and reviews line by line the details in order to determine the customer's responsibility and insurance responsibility.
• Completes a high-balance investigation to find new ways to prevent bad billings by researching insurance plans and insurance information. Makes outbound calls to insurance companies to inquire about the status of unpaid self-pay claims.
• Solves issues with insurance checks that go directly to the customers but belong to National Vision (NVI) by calling out to the customers to explain their balances owed.

• Bilingual - Spanish (Required)

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

· For short distances for short durations

· Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

· During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

· Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

· During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

· Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

· Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Hand Tasks

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

· Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

· Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

· Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

· Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.title: Head of Brand
jobs.description:
HEAD OF BRAND



You'll own how Firecrawl shows up in the world: the positioning, the voice, the social presence, the launch copy, and everything in between. Right now, we're one of the fastest-growing developer tools on the internet. This role is about making sure the world knows it, understands it, and chooses us over everything else.



Salary Range: $244,000–$277,000 USD/year

Equity Range: Competitive equity. Details shared during the process.

Location: San Francisco, CA (SF HQ). On-site, five days a week.

Job Type: Full-Time

Experience: 4+ years owning brand at a developer-facing or technical product company

Work Authorization: Must be authorized to work in the United States. We're not able to sponsor US visas right now, though that may change down the line.




ABOUT FIRECRAWL

Firecrawl is the easiest way to turn the web into data AI agents can use. One API call converts any URL into clean, LLM-ready markdown or structured data. It's the boring-hard problem everyone building with LLMs eventually hits, solved.

We hit 8 figures in ARR in year one and more than doubled it in year two. We have 180k+ GitHub stars, putting us in the top 50 repositories of all time, and developers, agents, and category-defining AI companies build on us every day. Growth like this is rare, and we're just getting started.

We're a small team punching far above our weight, working out of SF HQ and our new Toronto Hub. Everyone here owns a real piece of the product and company, end to end, and runs it themselves. No hiding behind process or headcount.

This is a place for people who want to work at the frontier: an AI company building the infrastructure other AI companies run on, not one bolting AI onto an existing product. We move fast, go deep, and are building the tools superintelligence will rely on to gather data from the web.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Firecrawl's brand positioning end to end, from how we describe ourselves on the homepage to how we show up in competitive comparisons and LLM recommendations

 - Write and ship launch copy, product announcements, website updates, and social posts that actually land with a technical audience

 - Grow and manage our presence on X and LinkedIn. Not just posting, but building a community and a point of view

 - Run competitive analysis and translate it into messaging that differentiates us clearly, without marketing-speak

 - Partner directly with founders and product to align brand with roadmap and GTM priorities

 - Shape the content calendar and own the cadence of what goes out across every channel

 - Think about discoverability beyond SEO, including how LLMs surface and recommend tools like ours




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You understand how developers think. Not just what they do, but how they evaluate tools, what they distrust, and what makes them share something with their team. You've built brand for a developer-facing product before and you have receipts

 - You're a writer first. The best brand work here will be in words: short-form, sharp, opinionated. You write copy that sounds like a smart person talking, not a marketing team hedging

 - You've driven organic growth. You've moved the needle on search visibility and social reach for a technical product, and the numbers hold up when we check them in Ahrefs

 - You're comfortable working directly with founders. No brand committee. No approval chain. You'll sit close to the people making product decisions and be expected to have a strong point of view on how we talk about what we're building

 - You think about LLMs as a distribution channel. You understand that discoverability now includes AI tools recommending products, and you know how to write for that world

Backgrounds that often do well: in-house brand at a developer tools or infra company, head of marketing at an early-stage API startup, founding marketer who owned everything from positioning to social.




WHAT WE'RE NOT LOOKING FOR

 - Brand strategists who hand off execution to someone else

 - People who measure success in impressions and engagement rate over organic growth and real developer mindshare

 - Anyone who needs a brand playbook handed to them before they can start




A NOTE ON PACE

We operate at an absurd level of urgency because the window for what we're building won't stay open forever. If that excites you, keep reading. If it doesn't, no hard feelings, but this role probably isn't for you.




BENEFITS & PERKS




AVAILABLE TO ALL EMPLOYEES

 - Salary that makes sense: $244,000–$277,000 USD/year, based on impact, not tenure

 - Own a piece: Gain competitive equity in what you're helping build

 - Generous PTO: 15 days mandatory, anything after 24 days, just ask (holidays excluded). Take the time you need to recharge

 - Parental leave: 12 weeks fully paid, for all parents

 - Wellness stipend: $100 USD/month for the gym, therapy, massages, or whatever keeps you human

 - Learning & Development: Expense up to $1,000 USD/year toward anything that helps you grow professionally

 - Team offsites: A change of scenery, minus the trust falls

 - Sabbatical: 3 paid months off after 4 years, do something fun and new




AVAILABLE TO US-BASED FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Full coverage, no red tape: Medical, dental, and vision (100% for employees, 50% for partner and kids). No weird loopholes, just care that works

 - Life & Disability insurance: Employer-paid basic life and AD&D, short-term disability, and long-term disability. Coverage for life's curveballs

 - Virtual care and a health guide: Teladoc for the couch doctor visit, plus Rightway to answer coverage questions and fight billing errors for you

 - Mental health: Talkspace, therapy and psychiatry on your schedule

 - Fertility and family building: Carrot, covering you and your partner

 - EAP: Free confidential counseling, legal and financial consults, and online will prep through Guardian

 - 401(k) plan: Retirement might be a ways off, but future-you will thank you

 - Pre-tax benefits: HSA, FSA, and commuter benefits to help your wallet out a bit

 - Supplemental options: Extra life and AD&D, accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity, plus pet, legal, and identity protection through MetLife




AVAILABLE TO SF-BASED EMPLOYEES

 - SF HQ perks: Snacks, drinks, team lunches, intense ping pong, and peak startup energy

 - E-Bike transportation: A loaner electric bike to get you around the city, on us




INTERVIEW PROCESS

Application Review: Send us your work: examples of brand or copy you've owned, social presence you've grown, or positioning you've built. Add a quick note on why Firecrawl, and what you'd want to change about how we show up today.

Intro Chat (~25 min): A quick conversation to get to know each other before we go deep. We'll talk about what you've built, your instincts on developer brand, and what you'd prioritize first. Time for your questions too.

Deep Dive Chat (~45 min): Walk us through a real example: a time you owned positioning for a technical product and it worked. Then we'll dig into a live scenario: how would you differentiate Firecrawl against our closest competitors? Come ready to think out loud. We care about taste and reasoning, not a rehearsed pitch.

Founder Chat (~25 min): Culture, pace, ownership, and how you like to work. Time for your questions too.

Paid Work Trial (~40 Hours): Work on a real brand problem with the team: a positioning rewrite, a launch brief, or a social content sprint. Paid at a contractor rate. We evaluate on taste, sharpness, and speed. Remote-friendly, and we'll flex around your current commitments.

Decision: We move fast after the trial.



If you want to own the brand of one of the fastest-growing developer tools on the internet, and you have the writing and instincts to back it up, this is your shot.

👉 Apply now.

jobs.title: Generator Logistics Specialist
jobs.description:
At PEARCE, we've got a career for you!

Pearce is a leading technology-enabled provider of asset management solutions for mission-critical electromechanical infrastructure throughout North America. Pearce provides technical maintenance, repair, operations, and engineering services for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, backup power generators, battery energy storage systems (BESS), critical cooling systems, and other electrical and mechanical infrastructure across end markets such as renewable energy, telecom, and data centers. Founded in 1998, Pearce has more than 4,000 employees and 28 locations across the U.S. Pearce is a wholly owned subsidiary of CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm. To learn more about Pearce visit http://www.pearce-services.com.

Your Impact

The Generator Logistics Specialist plays a key role in supporting generator operations by managing the procurement, inventory, warehousing, and logistics of parts, materials, rental generators, and load banks. This position is responsible for ensuring parts and equipment are sourced accurately, competitively, and on time to support field technicians, operations teams, and commercial customers.

The Generator Logistics Specialist will manage the procurement process for assigned regions across the United States, including obtaining and evaluating vendor quotes, monitoring pricing and lead times, coordinating purchase orders, tracking shipments, and maintaining accurate work-order and inventory records.

This position will also support commercial accounts by coordinating parts and pricing for customer proposals and ordering approved materials. In addition, the Specialist will manage warehouse activities, including receiving, organizing, cycle counting, pulling, and shipping parts, as well as coordinating the logistics of rental generators and load banks.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, responsive, and comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.

Core Responsibilities

Procurement & Vendor Management

• Review parts-to-be-ordered queues and ensure required materials are sourced and ordered in a timely manner.

• Request and evaluate vendor quotes based on price, availability, lead time, and operational requirements.

• Prepare and submit parts orders to approved vendors.

• Request purchase orders through GENPOR and maintain supporting quotes, order confirmations, and invoices.

• Establish and maintain relationships with new and existing vendors throughout the United States.

• Identify sourcing opportunities that improve pricing, availability, and lead times while supporting Pearce's operational needs.

• Monitor open purchase orders and proactively address delays, shortages, backorders, or other supply issues.

• Respond promptly to urgent parts and material requests from Operations and field technicians.

Inventory & Warehouse Operations

• Receive incoming parts and materials and verify shipments for quantity and accuracy.

• Add received parts to inventory and maintain accurate inventory records.

• Maintain appropriate stock levels for commonly used parts and materials.

• Perform regular cycle counts and investigate inventory discrepancies.

• Maintain a clean, organized, safe, and efficient warehouse environment.

• Properly label, organize, and stock parts and materials on warehouse shelves.

• Pull, package, and ship parts to technicians, customers, and project locations as required.

• Maintain accurate inventory and shipment information within applicable systems and spreadsheets.

• Ensure warehouse activities are performed in accordance with applicable safety and OSHA requirements.

Order & Work Order Management

• Review and maintain the Generator Parts Dashboard and associated queues to monitor all open parts orders.

• Track incoming shipments and update work orders with current shipping and delivery information.

• Ensure work orders are updated accurately and consistently throughout the procurement process.

• Verify that invoices and supporting documentation are attached to the appropriate orders and match received goods.

• Maintain accurate records of orders, shipments, invoices, inventory, and outstanding items.

• Communicate order status, delays, and potential issues to Operations and other stakeholders.

Commercial Account Support

• Obtain vendor quotes and pricing information needed to develop commercial customer proposals.

• Coordinate parts requirements and pricing for commercial service opportunities.

• Order parts and materials following customer approval of commercial proposals.

• Track customer-approved orders through delivery and ensure appropriate documentation is maintained.

• Partner with Operations, Sales, and other internal teams to support timely execution of commercial customer work.

Generator & Load Bank Logistics

• Coordinate the scheduling and logistics of rental generators and load banks.

• Track the location, availability, deployment, and return of rental equipment.

• Coordinate equipment movement with Operations, technicians, vendors, and project teams.

• Ensure rental generators and load banks are available when required to support customer and operational needs.

• Maintain accurate documentation related to equipment rentals and logistics.

Key Performance Expectations

• Effectively manage the procurement process for assigned regions across the United States.

• Maintain accurate and timely updates for work orders, procurement queues, and generator parts dashboards.

• Maintain high levels of warehouse organization, inventory accuracy, and cleanliness.

• Secure competitive pricing and appropriate lead times while maintaining strong vendor relationships.

• Minimize procurement delays that could negatively impact technicians, projects, or customers.

• Provide timely and accurate support for commercial customer proposals and approved parts orders.

• Effectively coordinate rental generator and load bank logistics.

• Maintain accurate purchasing, inventory, shipment, and invoice documentation.

• Provide responsive support to Operations and field teams.

Core Qualifications

• High school diploma or equivalent required.

• Previous experience in procurement, purchasing, sourcing, logistics, warehouse operations, inventory management, or supply chain preferred.

• Understanding of basic procurement and supply-chain processes.

• Strong organizational and time-management skills with exceptional attention to detail.

• Ability to manage multiple orders, requests, deadlines, and priorities simultaneously.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to compare vendor pricing, availability, and lead times.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to communicate effectively with vendors, technicians, Operations, Sales, and other internal stakeholders.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and the ability to learn inventory, procurement, and work-order management systems.

• Experience using inventory, ERP, purchasing, or work-order management software preferred.

• Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative team.

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to respond quickly to urgent operational needs.

• Commitment to maintaining accurate records and following established purchasing and inventory processes.

• Ability to comply with applicable OSHA and workplace safety requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting generator, critical power, electrical, field service, or equipment-service operations.

• Experience coordinating rental equipment or field-service logistics.

• Experience working with multiple vendors and sourcing parts across multiple geographic regions.

• Experience supporting commercial proposals, customer-approved purchases, or service-related parts procurement.

• Familiarity with generator parts, electrical components, load banks, or related critical-power equipment.

jobs.title: Builder
jobs.description:
Artisan · Full-time · In person in San Francisco or New York

Salary: $130,000–$230,000 USD annually. Equity: 0.08%–0.20%. US visa sponsorship available.


BUILD AI PRODUCTS FROM THE FIRST IDEA TO PRODUCTION

Artisan builds AI employees that take on real work. We're looking for Builders who can understand a customer problem, decide what the product should do, design the experience, and ship the code.

You'll own that whole process. You'll work directly with our CEO, Jaspar, and use your product judgment, design taste, and engineering ability to turn an unclear problem into something customers can use. Our ambition gives you plenty to build. Your judgment determines what deserves to ship first.

You should enjoy the responsibility that comes with that freedom. We expect you to make decisions, test them with customers, and stay accountable for the product after launch.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Talk to customers, study how they work, and identify problems worth solving. Bring a clear view of what matters and why.

 - Shape the product: write the spec, design the interface, make the tradeoffs, and keep the scope focused enough to ship quickly.

 - Build and ship production features in TypeScript and React. Use AI coding tools to move faster while understanding, reviewing, and testing the code you release.

 - Follow the result through to actual use. Watch where customers struggle, investigate failures, and improve the experience.

 - Maintain what you build. Fix bugs, handle edge cases, and make the system easier for the next engineer to understand.

 - Work closely with the rest of the team when your product touches shared infrastructure, AI behavior, or customer workflows.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've personally taken a product or substantial feature from an idea to production. You can explain the customer problem, your decisions, and what happened after launch.

 - You can ship TypeScript and React in an existing codebase without constant direction. You understand the code well enough to debug it when AI tooling gets something wrong.

 - You have strong product and design judgment. You care about how an interface works as well as how it looks.

 - You know outbound sales from experience: researching prospects, sending campaigns, handling replies, and selling a product. You can spot where the tools get in the way.

 - You take initiative and can defend a product decision, hear criticism, and change course when the evidence calls for it.

 - You move quickly and take responsibility for quality, maintenance, and the customer outcome.

You may have founded a company, worked as a sales engineer, or moved from sales into building software. Those are useful paths into this role. The strongest evidence is work you've shipped and can explain in detail.


USEFUL ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE

A sales, CRM, or outbound product with real users would be valuable. So would a public body of work: shipped products, a GitHub repository, or a technical write-up that shows how you think and build.


HOW WE WORK

This role is based in our San Francisco or New York office, in person five or more days per week, and reports to Jaspar. Expect a small team, short feedback cycles, direct communication, and high standards.

You'll have substantial freedom to choose an approach and the responsibility to make it work. We value people who surface problems early, share useful feedback, and care about the details of what they ship.


INTERVIEW PROCESS

 1. A 15-minute conversation with Jaspar.

 2. A paid, 48-hour take-home: design and ship a real feature for Ava.

 3. A 60-minute review with our founders and an engineer.

 4. A 30-minute conversation in person.

We can move from first conversation to offer in three to five days. When applying, share a product you personally built and explain what you owned.


ABOUT ARTISAN

Artisan builds AI employees that take on real work. Our first three are Ava, our outbound AI BDR; Aaron, our inbound AI SDR; and Aria, our AI account executive. Our broader mission is to build AI employees that can take responsibility for work across many roles and industries.

jobs.description:
Job Duties

• Operate all equipment. • Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler. • Prepare product. • Receive and process telephone orders. • Take inventory and complete associated paperwork. • Clean equipment and facility approximately daily. • Deliver product by car and then to door of customer. Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver’s license with safe driving record meeting company standards. Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. Must pass a background check and have open availability.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions. Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person. Ability to train and lead.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator). Must be able to make correct monetary change. Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed. Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen. Ability to maintain cost controls.

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area. Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO: Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks. In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas. Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside. Fumes from food odors. Exposure to cornmeal dust. Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler. Hot surfaces/tools from over up to 500 degrees or higher. Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING: Talking and hearing on the telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks. Depth perception. Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERMENTS: The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work along and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

STANDING: Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile “bricks” with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36” and 48”.

WALKING: Walking is generally in short distances for short durations.

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and the delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer’s location.

SITTING: Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

LIFTING: Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck. Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3’ x 1.5’. Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacking onto shelves up to 72” high.

CARRYING: Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves. Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried form the storage room to the front of the store. Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas, sides, and beverages while performing “walking” and “climbing” duties.

DRIVING: Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A team member may make several deliveries per shift.

PUSHING: Pushing is performed to move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24”-30” and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push. Trays may also be pulled.

CLIMBING: Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

STOOPING/BENDING: Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station. Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station. Duration of this position is approximately 40-45 seconds at a time, repeated continuously during the day. Forward bending is also present at the front counter when stocking ingredients.

CROUCHING/SQUATTING: Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

REACHING: Reaching is performed continuously; up, down, and forward. Workers reach above 72” occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves. Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes. Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

HAND TASKS: Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

We have continued to prove we “Put our People First” by making sure our work environment is safe and provides stability for you as a team member. The brand continues to deliver the “Power of Possible” to local Domino’s store owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores!
