jobs.title: Closing Delivery Driver(06273) - 200 A W 29 ST
jobs.description:
The Night Shift is where the money is!!! Domino's is Hiring Late Night Closing Delivery Drivers. Perfect as a second job, student financial support for school loans, or extra money to customize your ride.

Duties include

• Showing up on time for scheduled shifts
• Greeting customers
• Order taking over the phone and at the counter
• Cash handling
• Delivering orders to customers
• Communicating professionally with all team members
• Cleaning floors, ceilings, walls, shelves, sinks, dishes, restrooms, equipment, walk-in, refrigeration units, lobby area, and office area as needed
• Following all image and uniform standards
• Following all food and safety procedures

Must be available most weekends and holidays until roughly 1 and 2am.

Cannot be unavailable for your scheduled shift(s) due to inclement weather.

Drivers must be 18 years of age and have a driver's license in good standing for at least 1 year, proof of insurance and registration, a reliable, well-maintained vehicle, and be able to pass a standard background and motor vehicle records check.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans/bags, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried two at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients, as well as while washing dishes.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Billing
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Comfy lets people build creative workflows that combine open-source models running on our GPUs with paid APIs from model providers. Every run has a cost. Customers need to understand what they’re spending, and we need to charge accurately as models, prices, and products change.

You’ll own the engineering behind that: how we meter usage, collect payments, manage credits and subscriptions, and protect against financial abuse. You’ll make billing dependable for customers and give the team the tools to launch new pricing models with confidence.

Our billing stack uses Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, Stripe, and Metronome, alongside Python and Kubernetes across the broader platform. You’ll evolve an existing system, work across service boundaries, and take changes from design through production.

What you’ll do

 - Capture usage reliably. Build metering for GPU compute and partner model APIs. Handle delayed events, retries, and partial failures so every billable event is recorded once and attributed to the right workspace.

 - Own the payment lifecycle. Improve checkout, subscriptions, credit top-ups, plan and seat changes, prorations, refunds, and failed-payment recovery. Keep Stripe, Metronome, and our application state consistent when events arrive late or systems fail halfway through.

 - Reconcile charges, payments, and credits. Build automated checks across usage records, invoices, payments, and credit balances. Detect discrepancies, give operators an audit trail, and recover safely when a payment succeeds but credits never arrive. Own production reliability and turn incidents into lasting improvements.

 - Make new pricing easier to ship. Build reusable pricing and entitlement systems for individual creators, teams, and enterprise customers. Make changes safe for existing subscribers as we introduce new models, products, and plans.

 - Limit financial abuse. Improve spend controls and detection of suspicious usage, payment fraud, and credit abuse. Work with Support and Finance on disputes and recovery while keeping checkout and legitimate usage smooth.

 - Give customers and teammates clear answers. Partner with product and frontend engineers on billing experiences, and build tools that let Support, Sales, and Finance investigate charges and resolve issues safely.

You might be a good fit if you

 - Have built and operated billing or payments systems in production, with meaningful ownership of usage metering, credits, or consumption-based pricing.

 - Have integrated Stripe directly and worked through subscription changes, invoices, webhooks, and payment failures beyond the happy path.

 - Can reason carefully about money across distributed systems: idempotency, concurrent updates, reconciliation, rounding, and recovery after partial failure. You can explain how you found and prevented a real billing error.

 - Are a strong backend engineer with experience in relational data modeling and reliable APIs. You can learn our stack and work across services to solve a customer problem.

 - Care about the experience behind the numbers. You can explain technical tradeoffs to Finance, Product, and Support and use their feedback to build better systems.

 - Take ownership from problem definition through rollout and operation. You use AI development tools effectively and verify their output with the care that systems handling money require.

Bonus if you have

 - Worked with Metronome, Orb, or a similar metering platform.

 - Built durable workflows with Temporal.

 - Billed GPU infrastructure or model APIs, tracked provider costs, or built systems for changing rate cards and per-request margins.

 - Built spend limits or defenses against card testing, chargeback abuse, or trial and promotional-credit abuse.

 - Improved international checkout, payment-method coverage, or payment authorization rates.

 - Used ComfyUI, contributed to open source, or built tools for creative professionals.




ABOUT COMFY

Comfy (https://www.comfy.org) is the AI creation engine for visual professionals who demand control over every model, every parameter, and every output. The most powerful workflow engine for visual AI.

Unlike tools that hide everything behind a prompt box, Comfy lets you connect models, processing steps, and outputs on a canvas where every decision is visible and every step is inspectable. It gives you the building blocks to create workflows nobody's imagined yet, and share them with everyone.

What started as an open-source project in 2023 now has 4 million users, 60,000+ community-built nodes, and 150,000+ daily downloads. It's used by artists, filmmakers, game studios, designers, researchers, and VFX houses, including teams at OpenAI, Netflix, Amazon Studios, Ubisoft, EA, and Tencent.

We're a small, intense team in San Francisco. Our team comes from Stability AI and Google, and many contributed to the ComfyUI ecosystem long before working here. Low ego, high ownership. We work hard and demand a lot of each other, but we have fun. Everyone here is building something meaningful that will end up being our life's work.

If this mission excites you and you view yourself as top-tier talent, your future latent self is waiting for you at Comfy.

Check out our Github (https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI) and blog (https://blog.comfy.org). We recently raised $30M at a $500M valuation. The round was led by Craft, with participation from Pace Capital, Chemistry, TruArrow, and others.

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

JOB REQUIREMENTS

You must be 16 years of age or older.

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to:

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

Additional Job Details

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24 - 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72 occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.

Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.title: Senior Product Analytics Engineer - Ads
jobs.description:
About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

Ads is one of the fastest-growing and most strategically important parts of Faire's business, and the Ads Data team — now three years old — is entering a period of hypergrowth. As a product analytical engineer, you will own the end-to-end ads data foundation and models. You will partner closely with cross-functional teams in Product, Engineering, ML Applied Sciences, and Strategy & Analytics (S&A) to support product launches and roadmaps by designing and building data capabilities that inform and drive insights. You will lead the path in using AI to boost productivity and transform how analytical engineering operates—leveraging AI to streamline data pipeline development and operations, improve data consumption workflows, and automate routine analytical tasks. In this role, you'll see a direct link between your work, company growth, and user satisfaction.

Join us and be part of a team that values data-driven innovation and excellence.

What you’ll do

The ideal candidate will possess a perfect blend of analytics and data engineering expertise, along with strong skills in developing and supporting large-scale, high-performance data storage and processing systems. They should have a proven track record of collaborating with key stakeholders to execute on company-wide data initiatives.

• Lead the design, implementmentation, and optimization of end-to-end and scalable data pipelines and models for a domain defining the architecture, feature requirements, roadmap.

• Collaborate with engineers, product managers, S&A, and ML applied scientists to translate business requirements into production-grade data systems and insights.

• Build and maintain data infrastructure, pipelines, and models that ensure data quality, consistency, and accessibility for analytical workflows.

• Redefine how we build, maintain, and scale data systems by embedding AI into our daily workflows.

• Mentor team members on best practices for scalable data engineering and quantitative problem-solving.

• Ensure and promote data quality standards for accurate and reliable insights.

• Embrace emerging technologies with enthusiasm.

Qualifications

• 4+ years experience in analytics & data engineering roles focused on data modeling, large-scale data processing, and tool development for analytics or data science use cases. Preferred experiences within Ads domain.

• Demonstrated communication and leadership skills, with a history of initiating and steering successful projects across multiple stakeholders.

• Production-level development experience in Python.

• Strong SQL skills with demonstrable competencies in designing well-architected data models and optimizing query performance.

• Deep experience and knowledge of data warehousing concepts, ETLs, big data technologies, and analytics platforms.

• Experience with Airflow, Docker, DBT or similar analytics workflow tools.

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Math, Physics, or a related technical field.

jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team helps advance our mission by tackling novel legal issues in AI. Our team brings together professionals across technology, privacy, intellectual property, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation. Our regulatory compliance work turns legal requirements into practical programs that support responsible AI development and deployment.



About the Role

As a Legal Program Manager focused on regulatory compliance, you will build and manage cross-functional programs that translate counsel’s guidance into practical, sustainable operations. Your initial focus may include content moderation and/or frontier AI governance, with the mix shaped by team priorities and your strengths.

You will partner with internal and external counsel, other legal program managers, and technical and business teams to coordinate implementation, evidence collection, reporting, and ongoing compliance. You’ll build repeatable systems that scale across regulations, products, and jurisdictions, helping teams navigate emerging requirements with clarity and sound judgment.

This full-time role is based in San Francisco, CA, or New York, NY.



In this role, you will:

 - Lead regulatory compliance programs end to end: define scope, owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, and escalation paths, and drive execution with counsel and cross-functional partners.

 - Translate counsel’s regulatory guidance into repeatable workflows, controls, and documentation. Depending on your portfolio, this may include content moderation disclosures, transparency reporting, reporting and appeals workflows, or frontier AI model launch readiness, evaluation and risk-management evidence, and incident reporting.

 - Build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, User Operations, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC), Global Affairs, Communications, and Go-to-Market to align program priorities and deliverables.

 - Support regulatory inquiries, audits and investigations with counsel, organizing evidence and responses to support timely, accurate communication and reporting.

 - Identify execution risks and compliance gaps, track remediation, and escalate blockers. Establish clear success measures and operating cadences, keeping legal conclusions subject to counsel’s review.



You might thrive in this role if you:

jobs.title: Sr. Growth Engineer
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Comfy has millions of users and one of the largest open-source ecosystems in generative AI. Comfy Cloud gives that community a zero-setup way to create with ComfyUI, but we are still early in building the product-led growth engine around it.

We’re looking for a senior full-stack engineer to own that engine.

You will find the biggest opportunities in signup, onboarding, activation, monetization, and retention; turn them into hypotheses; build the experiments yourself; and use the results to decide what we ship, iterate, or kill.

This is not a role where a PM hands you a finished specification. You will work closely with Product, Design, Data, Marketing, and the founders, but you should be able to take an ambiguous growth problem from data and user insight all the way to production code and a defensible decision.

Your output is not tickets completed. It is more users reaching meaningful value, becoming paying customers, and continuing to create with Comfy.



What You’ll Do

Own experiments end to end: identify an opportunity, form a hypothesis, define the primary metric and guardrails, build the experience, instrument it, launch it, analyze the result, and make the ship-or-kill decision.

 - Improve the full Comfy Cloud journey, including account creation, first workflow, first successful output, templates, local-to-cloud adoption, credits, upgrade flows, billing, collaboration, sharing, and retention.

 - Build across the stack—from polished frontend experiences to backend services, APIs, data models, experiment assignment, billing logic, and lifecycle integrations.

 - Own measurable product outcomes such as activation, time to first value, free-to-paid conversion, retained usage, expansion, and revenue, while protecting reliability, user trust, and compute economics.

 - Query product data yourself and investigate user behavior without waiting for an analyst to translate it for you.

 - Talk with users and learn from Comfy’s community when quantitative data does not explain what is happening.

 - Build the minimum experimentation infrastructure needed to move quickly with trustworthy results: feature flags, exposure logging, event instrumentation, experiment health checks, and reusable patterns.

 - Turn successful experiments into durable, production-quality product experiences.

 - Raise the growth-engineering bar by documenting what the team learns and helping other engineers run better experiments.
   
   

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

 - Have 6+ years of software engineering experience and are strong across both frontend and backend development.

 - Have personally owned an activation, conversion, retention, or revenue metric—and can explain how your work moved it.

 - Have run real product experiments from hypothesis through analysis, including experiments that failed or produced ambiguous results.

 - Can work without a detailed specification. You know how to combine data, user insight, product judgment, and technical constraints into a sensible next bet.

 - Are comfortable building user-facing experiences in TypeScript and a modern frontend framework, as well as backend services and APIs. Experience with Vue is useful, but strong fundamentals matter more than an exact stack match.

 - Can use SQL and product analytics tools to explore funnels, cohorts, experiment results, and unexpected behavior.

 - Understand experiment fundamentals: assignment, exposure, primary metrics, guardrails, sample-size tradeoffs, novelty effects, and segmentation.

 - Have excellent product judgment and care about UX quality—not just whether the code works.

 - Move quickly while knowing when an experiment can be lightweight and when billing, identity, privacy, or core product architecture demands more rigor.

 - Thrive in a small, intense team with high ownership, low ego, and a fast clock.



Bonus Points

 - You have built growth systems for a PLG, developer-tool, creator-tool, or usage-based SaaS product.

 - You have worked on onboarding, templates, collaboration loops, referrals, pricing and packaging, subscriptions, credits, usage metering, or Stripe integrations.

 - You have built or introduced experimentation infrastructure rather than only consuming an established platform.

 - You understand the unusual dynamics of growing an open-source product alongside a commercial cloud offering.

 - You use ComfyUI or other professional creative-AI tools and have opinions about making their power more approachable without flattening it.

 - You use AI development tools as a normal part of how you explore and ship.



What This Role Is Not

 - A marketing-engineering role limited to landing pages and SEO.

 - An analytics-engineering role focused primarily on pipelines and dashboards.

 - A feature factory where Product decides what to build and Data decides whether it worked.

 - A research role that produces experiment ideas for other engineers to implement.



What Success Looks Like

In your first three months, you will understand the Comfy Cloud funnel, establish trustworthy baselines, identify the largest points of friction, and ship your first experiments.

Within six months, you will own a repeatable experiment cadence, have produced measurable improvements to at least one company-level growth metric, and have made it substantially easier for the team to launch and evaluate new growth ideas.

Within twelve months, Comfy will have a stronger self-serve growth engine—and a body of accumulated knowledge about what helps creators discover value, convert, and stay—because of the systems and experiments you built.




ABOUT COMFY

Comfy (https://www.comfy.org) is the AI creation engine for visual professionals who demand control over every model, every parameter, and every output. The most powerful workflow engine for visual AI.

Unlike tools that hide everything behind a prompt box, Comfy lets you connect models, processing steps, and outputs on a canvas where every decision is visible and every step is inspectable. It gives you the building blocks to create workflows nobody's imagined yet, and share them with everyone.

What started as an open-source project in 2023 now has 4 million users, 60,000+ community-built nodes, and 150,000+ daily downloads. It's used by artists, filmmakers, game studios, designers, researchers, and VFX houses, including teams at OpenAI, Netflix, Amazon Studios, Ubisoft, EA, and Tencent.

We're a small, intense team in San Francisco. Our team comes from Stability AI and Google, and many contributed to the ComfyUI ecosystem long before working here. Low ego, high ownership. We work hard and demand a lot of each other, but we have fun. Everyone here is building something meaningful that will end up being our life's work.

If this mission excites you and you view yourself as top-tier talent, your future latent self is waiting for you at Comfy.

Check out our Github (https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI) and blog (https://blog.comfy.org). We recently raised $30M at a $500M valuation. The round was led by Craft, with participation from Pace Capital, Chemistry, TruArrow, and others.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Front Desk Operations
jobs.description:
The Cal Alumni Association (CAA) provides all Cal graduates with rewarding connections to the university, to fellow alums, and to current students. Founded by the original graduates of the University of California in 1872, the Cal Alumni Association today represents more than half a million alums living throughout the world.

Our mission is to cultivate a lifelong relationship with our alma mater by connecting and inspiring alums, students, and the campus community through meaningful and inclusive opportunities. We foster a culture that celebrates diversity, creates a sense of belonging, and advances equity.

Senior Manager, Front Desk Operations

Department:

Facilities Operations

Reports To:

Senior Director of Facilities Operations

Classification:

Full-Time, Exempt

Location:

Alumni House, UC Berkeley Campus

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Front Desk Operations is a vital professional leadership role responsible for establishing, cultivating, and maintaining an elite customer service ecosystem at the California Alumni Association (CAA). Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Facilities Operations, this role serves as the premier authority on front-of-house hospitality, workspace operational efficiency, and cross-functional operational alignment. A primary focus of this role is the creation, delivery, and continuous evaluation of a comprehensive hospitality training framework that spans across multiple professional levels including permanent operational staff, contractors, temporary employees, and undergraduate student workers. The Senior Manager acts as a strategic process driver: designing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), spearheading campus and inter-organizational communication pipelines, optimizing and administrating front desk supply budgets, and partnering directly with CAA Engagement Teams and UC Berkeley administrators to deliver high-level visitor experiences.

Core Responsibilities

• Hospitality Strategy & Front-of-House Training Excellence (45%)

• Hospitality Framework Design: Build, launch, and refine a standardized advanced hospitality program rooted in modern concierge standards, to ensure elite service delivery for visiting alumni, donors, dignitaries, and university administrators.

• Comprehensive Workforce Onboarding: Author and deliver a mandatory hospitality and service-excellence training curriculum tailored to various user levels, ensuring consistent execution across permanent staff, temporary workforce additions, and student support teams. Guide the employee onboarding and institutional onboarding process for new hires at various levels.

• Performance Auditing & Coaching: Establish service milestones, execute regular service evaluations, and provide targeted coaching to front desk staff to maintain maximum customer satisfaction and professional presence.

• Desk Management & Resource Workflows: Direct the strategic master schedule for front-of-house student and employee coverage, structuring smooth shift transitions, policy adherence, and proper handover routines across all employee groups.

• SOP Engineering, Emergency Communication & Risk Readiness (25%)

• Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs): Research, draft, and issue modernized front-of-house operational manuals included but not limited to; facility operational sequences, access control, guest reception mechanics, and technical incident reporting.

• Emergency Communication & Crisis Command: Serve as the front-of-house emergency coordinator. Maintain direct, active linkage with the UC Berkeley Police Department (UCPD), Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S), and university safety officials to develop and deploy real-time building evacuation and emergency communication pipelines.

• Facilities Operations Monitoring: Continually assess the spatial environment of the lobby, reception corridors, and adjacent shared public spaces to preserve aesthetic upkeep, security compliance, and CAA quality brand alignment.

• Collaborative Team Coordination (15%)

• Cross-Functional Engagement Synergy: Collaborate closely with CAA Engagement teams to coordinate space readiness and utilization, specialized event support, and front-office branding transitions for high-impact events.

• Administrative Interface: Act as a central administrative liaison between the Alumni House operations department and various UC Berkeley campus divisions, building managers, and external vendors during large-scale collaborative traditions.

• Fiscal Administration & Supply Budgeting (15%)

• Budget Management: Develop, track, and balance the annual operational budget for front desk supplies, technology, signage materials, engagement and hospitality assets.

• Procurement Pipelines: Execute and audit purchasing and procurement with organizational finance department. Ensure alignment with organizational budgets, conduct vendor analysis, and control overhead expenditures.

Qualifications & Core Competencies

Required Education & Experience:

• Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution, or equivalent combination of advanced education and professional operational experience.

• A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience overseeing front-of-house operations, corporate hospitality, luxury guest services, or student affairs operations within a complex university or corporate setting.

• Proven experience authoring, implementing, and instructing a hospitality training program or customer service curriculum across a diverse, multi-tiered employee workforce.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

• Advanced procedural writing competence with a track record of translating organizational policies into scalable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

• Exceptional verbal and written communication skills; absolute poise and comfort interacting directly with senior university executives, governing board, executive level employees, institutional donors, and community leaders.

• Robust crisis management aptitude with previous experience executing facility-wide emergency communication drills or safety protocols.

• A working familiarity with basic fiscal administration, budgetary spreadsheets, and financial reporting and forecasting.

Preferred Experience:

Prior professional exposure to the UC campus ecosystem, institutional governance structures, or alumni relations is highly desired.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations (Medical Device)
jobs.description:
What is Motif?

Motif is a medical device startup based in Houston, Texas. We are designing and developing minimally invasive electronic solutions for serious mental health conditions. Powered by our patent-pending methods for wireless power and data transmission, our goal is to create the smallest implantable brain stimulator to treat people with mental health disorders.

We are an early-stage startup with funding from venture capital firms, grants, and private angel and founder investments.

Motif’s technology stack consists of a small implant that is wirelessly powered via magnetic fields from an external wearable transmitter, configured and controlled from a programming interface. It delivers novel stimulation therapy to cortical targets and will evolve to record biomarkers of symptoms, disease state, and therapy response.

Where are we going?

We are currently completing the development of our first minimally invasive neural stimulation system and preparing for future versions with additional functionality based on our platform technology.

About the Job

We are seeking candidates with a background in medical device manufacturing and operations (supply chain, purchasing, inventory management) to ensure that we have everything we need to build high quality medical devices on time. If you have a passion for building innovative medical technologies and helping others do the same, apply now to be part of our dedicated team.

You will manage our manufacturing function by selecting and implementing our inventory and manufacturing management software, working with engineering to write and refine our manufacturing processes, and managing a supply chain and multi-lab facility to build Class III innovative neural implant devices. This role will manage a small team of operators and operations team members to execute manufacturing and operations work.

This job is an ideal role for somebody well-versed in medical device manufacturing who wants to grow into broader operations management such as inventory, facilities, supply chain, and purchasing.

Job Location: Onsite in Houston, Texas.

Does this sound like you?

• Do you like creating systems and processes to help others do great work?

• Do you believe that openness and honesty are key to team success?

• Do you want to create a future where technology enables better mental healthcare?

If yes to the above, then you may love working with Motif as it is being built by highly dedicated people with passion for neurotechnology, clinical product development, and putting the patient first. We are looking for people with the same energy who will thrive in a high growth, high autonomy environment.

In this role, you will:

• Establish and refine processes to support high quality medical devices

• Continuously improve processes for handling equipment, calibration, maintenance, inventory management, and manufacturing records

• Work closely with engineering to validate and implement new processes or help refine existing processes for manufacturing

• Partner with engineering to identify and evaluate new potential processes

• Work with quality and engineering to conduct risk assessments (pFMEAs), monitor build quality, and inspected at appropriate control points

• Own the process validation strategy across the product lifecycle, including IQ/OQ/PQ planning, protocol authorship, execution, and summary reporting

• Participate in the Change Control Board (CCB) as the operations representative, reviewing proposed design, process, and material changes for manufacturing and inventory impact

• Onboard and manage software, tooling, and new manufacturing equipment and processes to support resource planning, part lifecycle management, and new manufacturing procedures

• Manage the team that manages supply chain by selecting suppliers, working with quality on effective supplier agreements, and monitoring supplier performance

• Run manufacturing and inventory operations

• Manage inventory and ensure full product and part traceability through receiving, inspection, and marking and labeling procedures

• Develop the build schedule and ensure builds are prioritized and changes are communicated to appropriate stakeholders

• Purchase supplies, tooling, and capital equipment for engineering and manufacturing according to our purchasing procedures

• Represent manufacturing/operations in weekly meetings and in a quality documentation reviews

• Manage and maintain the facility and team

• Ensure facilities are operational and safe by implementing and following OSHA guidelines and establishing and maintaining PPE requirements, safety markings, and more

• Oversee a team of manufacturing engineers, technicians, and operations/supply chain personnel, including hiring, onboarding, and performance management, and set work direction across the function

• Own the environmental controls and monitoring program for controlled manufacturing areas (e.g., cleanroom classification, particulate monitoring, gowning procedures) required for Class III device production

• Ensure manufacturing's adherence to the company's Quality Management System, including DHF/DMR contributions, CAPA participation, and audit readiness

• Occasionally travel to supplier conferences/trade shows such as MD&M West and/or to visit contract manufacturers and suppliers in Taiwan (a few times per year at most)

• This is not an exhaustive list of duties and you may be asked to perform different tasks if your role within or the objectives of the organization changes.

To be considered, you will need:

• 8+ years of experience in manufacturing

• 3+ years of experience in medical device manufacturing and cGMP manufacturing

• 2+ years of experience hiring and managing performance for teams of manufacturing engineers, technicians, and/or support staff

• Substantial experience working with manufacturing resource planning or enterprise resource planning software for the purpose of managing manufacturing operations and builds (work orders, sales orders, etc)

• Experience in manufacturing and design documentation development, including writing and improving manufacturing procedures, developing or identifying areas for in-process inspections and influencing design for manufacturability

• Some experience in purchasing, procurement or supply chain management

• Demonstrable strong written and verbal communication skills for cross-departmental coordination

• Experience working under a Quality Management system (ISO 13485/21 CFR Part 820), and working with both design files and manufacturing records

• To be available to work onsite full-time in our Houston, Texas office (relocation assistance available)

It is a bonus if you have:

• Experience managing or implementing a BSL Level II or stricter lab

• Experience with in-house sterilization and packaging

• Experience owning process validation (IQ/OQ/PQ) and FMEA/risk management activities for regulated products

Work Authorization Notice

Motif Neurotech hires only individuals who are authorized to work in the United States. At this time, visa sponsorship is not offered for this role.

Benefits*

We envision a world where everyone with a mental health disorder can get well and stay well, regardless of who you are, where you live, or how much money you make, and we are excited to build that future with you.

Let’s use our powers for good.

jobs.title: Staff Safety Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Description

Third Wave Automation is a rapidly growing startup that has demonstrated its core technology components, proven its market fit, and just closed its Series C funding. If you are excited about cutting edge machine learning, robotics that affects the real world, and want to join a company where your skills can have a huge impact, you’ll fit right in.

Third Wave Automation is applying modern machine learning to materials handling—delivering site-specific forklift navigation and infrastructure-free pallet handling that continuously adapts to changing floor configuration and warehouse demand.

Job Description

The Mission: Architecting Safety for Physical AI

At Third Wave Automation, we don’t just deploy technology; we transform how the world’s largest OEMs and logistics providers operate. Moving 3,000lb autonomous reach trucks with centimeter precision means that safety isn't just a regulatory hurdle—it is the bedrock of our product, our customer trust, and our entire business model.

We are looking for a Staff Safety Engineer to act as our primary technical authority on system safety and compliance. We do not want a "box-checker" or someone whose favorite phrase is "because the standard says so." We are looking for an innovator—a deeply technical engineer who understands why a standard exists and can propose novel, compliant architectures that accommodate the bleeding edge of Physical AI. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will have full autonomy. You will inherit a strong foundation, but you will have the absolute authority to refine, correct, or completely rebuild our frameworks if there is a better way.

How You Can Make an Impact

• Architect the Safety System: Partner directly with Product and Engineering leaders to weave safety into the DNA of our robotics platform. Your job isn't to slow them down; it’s to show them how to move fast, safely—pushing our systems to go above and beyond the baseline requirements.

• Industry Influence & Advocacy: Represent TWA on national and international standards committees. We are building tech that outpaces current regulations; you will advocate for and influence standards bodies to accommodate and safely regulate the next generation of embodied AI.

• AI-Augmented Execution: While AI will never dictate our safety architecture, we expect our leaders to be at the forefront of modern productivity. You will leverage generative AI and advanced tooling to parse dense regulatory updates, draft technical documentation, and streamline hazard analysis—acting as a massive force multiplier for your own output.

• Lead the Certification Vanguard: Own and drive the end-to-end certification processes for complex autonomous systems across hardware, software, and cybersecurity.

• The Voice of Trust: Act as the definitive safety authority for our Tier-1 OEM partners and customers. You will translate our rigorous safety architecture into customer confidence and business value.

• EHS Leadership: Safety starts at home. You will oversee our internal Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) programs, ensuring our field engineers, deployment teams, and lab staff have the right training, protocols, and protection to do their best work.

What You'll Do (Your First 90 Days and Beyond)

• Assess the Foundation: Conduct a deep-dive audit of our existing safety architecture, EHS programs, and compliance documentation. Identify immediate areas for improvement or complete reinvention.

• Build Cross-Functional Alliances: Establish strong partnerships with Product, Engineering, and Field Operations leaders to embed safety requirements smoothly into our development and deployment cycles.

• Drive Key Certifications: Take immediate ownership of ongoing certification processes (e.g., IEC 61508, ISO 13849, ISO 21434) and map out the strategy for future regulatory compliance.

• Engage with Standards Bodies: Begin representing Third Wave Automation in relevant industry committees, advocating for standards that align with the realities of modern embodied AI.

• Elevate EHS Protocols: Review and upgrade our internal Environmental, Health, and Safety training to ensure every TWA employee operates with the highest level of protection.

Qualifications

• 10+ Years of Deep Expertise: A decade or more of hands-on experience in safety engineering within robotics, autonomous systems, automotive, or heavy industrial automation.

• Regulatory Mastery: Deep, working knowledge of OSHA regulations and core autonomy standards, specifically IEC 61508, ISO 13849 (Parts 1 & 2), and ISO/SAE 21434 (Cybersecurity).

• The "First-Principles" Mindset: The technical depth to challenge engineering assumptions and propose innovative safety solutions rather than relying on outdated boilerplate compliance.

• AI Fluency: Comfortable leveraging LLMs and modern software tools to 10x your efficiency in research, technical writing, and workflow automation without compromising engineering rigor.

• Diplomacy & Gravitas: Proven experience participating in industry standards committees and the professional polish to influence C-suite executives, OEMs, and regulatory bodies.

• A "Builder's" Autonomy: The ability to operate in a high-growth startup environment where you are trusted to define the roadmap, not just execute someone else’s plan.

Preferred & Desired Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or higher in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.

• Deep experience navigating functional safety audits and successfully achieving safety certifications for complex hardware/software systems.

• Outstanding interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex safety standards into clear, actionable engineering requirements.

• Outstanding interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex safety standards into clear, actionable engineering requirements.

The pay range for this position is $166,000 - $249,000/yr+ benefits+equity; however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  Base pay information is based on market location.

More About Working Here

Our Core Values:

• Safety. We consider safety in everything we do.

• People. We care about our teammates as people.

• Encouragement. We encourage teaching, asking questions, and sharing opinions.

• Transparency. We are transparent and sincere in our actions.

A robust set of benefits and perks:

• Comprehensive benefits. Health, Dental, Vision, and a 401k matching program, to boot!

• Flexible working schedule. Be productive when you work best.

• Show & Tell. We love to learn from one another, and see the cool stuff everyone is working on!

• Meals are covered. Lunch is provided every day, and dinner for those evenings that run long.

• Stacks of snacks. Donuts are a main food group, and the snack shelf is always stocked with a wide variety of items.

• Great teammates. One of the best parts of working here!

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We value each person's expertise and experiences. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

All qualified applicants able to work in the United States are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor H-1 visas subject to fees required by the ‘Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers’ Presidential Proclamation dated September 21, 2025.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Strategy
jobs.description:
About Us

Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.

It is Kardigan’s mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan’s co-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020.

We have a cutting-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late-stage candidates, and an industry-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

At Kardigan, we are motivated by our values which guide how we work, interact, and achieve our goals. Driven by patients and their families, we are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients and prioritizing their needs above all else. We believe in being authentic—leading with truth to bring out the best in others by creating an environment where every person knows they will be fully accepted. With an eagerness to learn, we encourage the highest levels of curiosity and are open to changing our minds. We are committed to winning as a team with urgency, excellence, and intention, and support each other no matter what role we play or where we sit. Lastly, we strive to enable the impossible because patients are counting on us. We are not afraid to take risks to unlock innovation and advance scientific discoveries.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day.

About the Job

Job Title: Senior Director, Product Strategy

Level: Senior Director

Department: Product Strategy

Hiring Manager: Vice President, Product Strategy

Location: Princeton, NJ

Classification: Hybrid – On-site 4 days per week (Mon to Thurs)

Travel: Approximately 10–15% across Kardigan’s South San Francisco, Princeton, and Chicago sites

About the Team

Kardigan’s Product Strategy team sits at the intersection of science, clinical development, commercial, and corporate strategy. The team translates Kardigan’s pipeline of investigational cardiovascular therapies into clear product visions, target product profiles, value propositions, and lifecycle strategies — ensuring that every development decision is grounded in rigorous data, differentiated positioning, and long-term portfolio value creation.

Working hand-in-hand with Global Program Heads and colleagues across Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Regulatory, Commercial, Market Access, and Business Development, the team provides the fact base, analytics, and strategic framing that power Kardigan’s portfolio governance and investment decisions. Team members shape programs at their most important stages, help build new capabilities in competitive intelligence, forecasting, and market access, and ultimately ensure that our product strategies serve patients and their families above all else.

All Kardigan product candidates are investigational; references to launch and commercialization describe readiness planning for potential future approvals.

Job Overview

Kardigan is seeking a Senior Director, Product Strategy to serve as the product strategy lead for an assigned program within Kardigan’s portfolio of investigational cardiovascular therapies. Reporting to the Vice President, Product Strategy, this leader develops and drives the integrated product strategy for their assigned program — building the target product profile, value proposition, and differentiation strategy, and delivering the analyses and decision-support materials that inform program and portfolio decisions.

The Senior Director is the day-to-day product strategy partner to the Global Program Head and the cross-functional program team, leading through influence rather than direct authority. This leader executes competitive assessments, forecasting inputs, and scenario analyses in partnership with the function’s Centers of Excellence, prepares governance-ready recommendations for review by product strategy leadership, and drives assigned launch-readiness workstreams.

Main Responsibilities

Program Product Strategy Development

• Develop, maintain, and evolve the integrated product strategy for the assigned program, ensuring it reflects current clinical data, competitive dynamics, and portfolio priorities.

• Draft and iterate the target product profile (TPP), value proposition, and differentiation strategy for the assigned program, and drive cross-functional input and alignment on the evidence required to support them.

• Partner with Clinical Development and Medical Affairs on the assigned program to provide product strategy input into trial design, endpoint selection, and evidence-generation planning.

• Conduct scenario planning and trade-off analyses across indications, lines of therapy, and geographies for the assigned program, and frame options and implications for review by product strategy leadership and the Global Program Head.

• Maintain our evolving perspective on the competitive environment and generate insights leveraging continuous data generation and identifying issues to monitor.

Analysis & Decision Support

• Generate insights based on competitive intelligence. Build and maintain the program-level commercial fact base — market landscape, patient flow, unmet need, and competitive positioning — that supports portfolio decision-making and governance reviews.

• Own key forecast assumptions which will enable financial models, forecasting inputs, and program valuation analyses in partnership with the forecasting Center of Excellence to support stage-gate decisions, new indication assessments, and development plan modifications.

• Prepare clear, decision-ready materials and recommendations for portfolio governance forums, for review and sponsorship by product strategy leadership.

• Track key performance indicators and impact measures for the assigned program’s integrated product strategy and report progress, risks, and mitigation options.

• Support business development evaluations related to the assigned program or disease area, contributing market, competitive, and strategic analyses to due diligence efforts.

• Provide commercial perspectives that inform our individual new program decisions such as lifecycle management programs.

Launch-Readiness Support

• Partner with the commercial organization to develop and refine launch plan. Drive assigned workstreams within the cross-functional launch-readiness plan for the program, in anticipation of potential future approvals, coordinating deliverables and timelines across contributing functions.

• Work with Regulatory and Market Access to document regulatory pathway, pricing, and reimbursement considerations for the assigned program, drawing on the market access Center of Excellence.

• Own evolving go-to-market strategy globally; identifying new markets, sequencing entry and defining go-to-market model.

Cross-Functional Leadership

• Serve as the day-to-day product strategy partner to the Global Program Head and cross-functional Global Program team, leading through influence to drive alignment without direct authority.

• Facilitate resolution of cross-functional questions on program strategy, escalating conflicts and portfolio-level implications to product strategy leadership with clear options.

• Contribute to the Product Strategy function’s frameworks, templates, and ways of working, and may provide day-to-day guidance to analysts or Center of Excellence staff supporting the program.

About You

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year college or university in a scientific, health, or business discipline.

• 8+ years of experience in biotech, pharmaceutical, or life sciences strategy consulting, including direct experience supporting product, portfolio, or asset strategy for late stage clinical programs.

• Demonstrated experience developing core product strategy deliverables — target product profiles, value propositions, competitive assessments, or market landscape analyses — for one or more clinical-stage assets.

• Proven experience working cross-functionally with R&D, Commercial, Regulatory, and Market Access colleagues and leading workstreams through influence without direct authority.

• Strong analytical capability, including hands-on experience with financial modeling, forecasting, and program valuation.

• Strong scientific literacy and working knowledge of clinical development, regulatory pathways, and competitive dynamics.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of clear executive-level presentations.

• Ability to work on-site four days per week in Princeton, New Jersey with flexibility to travel approximately 10–15% across Kardigan’s South San Francisco, Princeton, and Chicago sites.

Preferred Qualifications

• Advanced degree (PhD, MD, PharmD, or MBA).

• Experience in cardiovascular preferred.

• Exposure to pre-launch or launch planning, including pricing and reimbursement or evidence-generation strategy development.

• Experience presenting to senior governance and influencing executive audiences.

• Experience mentoring junior team members and coordinating the work of analysts, consultants or matrixed contributors.

• Experience in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial biotech environment, with a strong patient-centric orientation and continuous-improvement mindset.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Kardigan is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace and consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, gender identity, gender expression, and sexual orientation), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and employment process.

Exact Compensation may vary based on skills, experience and location.

Pay range

$218,000—$284,000 USD

jobs.description:

jobs.description:
Role Summary

Join our team as Assistant Director of Wellbeing  supports the Director of Wellbeing in leading the strategic, financial, and operational performance of the  Wellness and Fitness  department. This role has primary responsibility for the consistent execution of daily operations, team leadership, scheduling, guest and member experience, service quality, retail performance, and administrative controls. The Assistant Director serves as the department leader in the Director's absence and works closely with resort leaders to deliver a seamless luxury experience while achieving revenue, profitability, and engagement.

As part of the Auberge family, we are looking for a dynamic facilities leader, who can manage budgets and capital funds, expenditure projects, preventative maintenance and energy conservation and have an eye for maintaining the highest of luxury standards in product finishes, timely and efficient remediations, standards and regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Please note that this is not an exhaustive list of everything that needs to be done. Within the Auberge family, our people always find new ways to look after the business, their guests, and their teammates. Within this, the key responsibilities for this position are:

Leadership and Daily Operations

• Provide visible, hands-on leadership throughout the Spa & Fitness, maintaining a consistent presence in guest and team areas and ensuring that daily operations reflect luxury service standards.
• Direct day-to-day spa operations, including front desk,, provider operations, spa attendants, housekeeping support, fitness programming, retail, and related guest services.
• Assume the responsibilities of the Director of Wellbeing in the Director’s absence and promptly elevate significant operational, guest, safety, financial, or team member matters.
• Partner with the Director to implement departmental strategy, policies, annual priorities, service initiatives, and continuous operational improvements.
• Participate as an active member of the resort management team, including daily and weekly meetings, cross-departmental planning, and Manager on Duty shifts as assigned.
• Maintain current Spa policies and procedures and reinforce company standards consistently and fairly.
• Develop and oversee a sophisticated, innovative fitness and movement programming aligned with the Resorts luxury wellness positioning

Guest and Member Experience

• Ensure guest, member and residences needs are anticipated and addressed courteously, promptly, and thoughtfully at every stage of the experience.
• Coach the team to act as caring problem solvers who are cooperative, accommodating, professional, and accountable.
• Monitor service quality through observation, role-playing, training, audits, and guest feedback; lead timely service recovery when expectations are not met.
• Build relationships with members and repeat guests, support membership tours and inquiries, and assist with account questions, requests, renewals, upgrades, and retention efforts.
• Coordinate spa services and fitness programs for groups, special events, retreats, and property activations in partnership with resort departments

Team Leadership and Development

• Support recruitment, interviewing, hiring, onboarding, training, scheduling, coaching, performance management, and professional development across Spa and Wellness roles.
• Directly manage designated operational teams, including Front Desk , and partner with department leads to support providers, spa attendants, housekeeping, fitness, and retail operations.

• Ensure team members have the supplies, equipment, uniforms, information, and training required to perform their roles safely and effectively.

Financial Performance and Revenue

• Understand how departmental operations affect property financial goals and manage daily activities to achieve or exceed budgeted revenue, labor, expense, retail, and profitability targets.
• Support and manage the fitness department budget while monitoring departmental performance and key business metrics fitness/wellbeing.
• Manage provider, front desk, attendant, and operational schedules to maximize booking opportunities, treatment room use, service availability, and labor productivity.
• Review daily business levels and adjust schedules, availability, and operating plans to improve revenue while controlling labor and other expenses.
• Support treatment, retail, membership, wellness program, and group sales through knowledgeable recommendations, effective merchandising, inventory availability, and team coaching.
• Assist the Director with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, expense review, capital planning, purchasing, and performance analysis.
• Monitor supplies, equipment, product inventory, loss prevention, and vendor services to maintain appropriate controls and achieve the best value for the company.

Spa Programming and Business Development

• Support the development and ongoing refinement of treatments, menus, wellness initiatives, and seasonal programming in response to guest needs and industry trends.
• Help identify opportunities to increase awareness, bookings, fitness revenue, retail sales, and guest participation while protecting service quality and operational capacity.
• Maintain productive relationships with practitioners, instructors, suppliers, and business partners and help evaluate performance, compliance, service quality, and value.

The starting range for this position is $95,000-$105.00. This is the pay rate for this position that Stanly Ranch reasonably expects to pay. Decisions regarding individual salaries will be based on a number of factors, such as experience and education.

Required Qualifications

• Minimum three years of progressive leadership experience in spa, wellness, luxury hospitality, or a closely related operation, including at least two years in a supervisory or management role.
• Demonstrated experience managing daily operations, guest service, team member scheduling, training, sales, and expense controls.
• Working knowledge of spa treatments, reservations, retail, fitness operations/programming, and luxury service standards.
• Experience maintaining applicable health, safety, sanitation, and licensing requirements.
• Strong administrative skills, including reporting, budgeting, project coordination, inventory management, and written communication.
• Ability to work a flexible schedule, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays, based on business needs.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience at a luxury hotel, resort, or Forbes-rated property.
• Experience with spa management, hotel property management, point-of-sale, scheduling, and productivity reporting
• systems.

Skills and Leadership Behaviors

• Clear, professional communication and strong interpersonal judgment.
• Calm, confident decision-making and the ability to perform under pressure.
• Strong organization, follow-through, attention to detail, and comfort managing competing priorities.
• Financial awareness and the ability to translate business needs into daily operating decisions.
• A collaborative leadership style grounded in fairness, discretion, accountability, and genuine care for guests and employees.
• Ability to coach teams, resolve concerns constructively, and maintain standards in a fast-paced environment.

Physical Demands

jobs.title: Motion Planning Engineer (PhD, Intern)
jobs.description:
About The Company

DiDi's autonomous driving unit was established in 2016 with the mission of developing Level 4 autonomous driving (AD) technology to make transportation safer and more efficient. In August 2019, the unit became an independent company, DiDi Autonomous Driving, dedicated to advanced AD R&D, product application, and business expansion. We believe integrating AD technology into a shared-mobility fleet will generate immense social value. By leveraging DiDi's specialized technology, operational expertise, and integrated ecosystem, we are positioned to build and operate a highly efficient, user-oriented autonomous fleet.

About The Role

We are seeking a motivated PhD graduate with a strong research background in motion planning, robotics, or autonomous systems. In this role, you will apply your expertise in algorithm design and system integration to help develop next-generation planning capabilities for autonomous vehicles.

Responsibilities

• Implement novel solutions for Behavioral Planning, enabling high-level decision-making for lane changes, merges, yields, and multi-agent interactions.

• Design and optimize motion planning algorithms that integrate geometry-based path reasoning and context-aware speed reasoning into smooth, safe trajectories.

• Develop and improve core geometry and velocity planning systems to ensure feasibility, compliance, and comfort across diverse driving scenarios.

• Model complex driving environments and agent behaviors to create a robust world representation for planning under uncertainty.

• Formulate cost functions and optimization frameworks that balance safety, comfort, and efficiency in trajectory selection.

• Analyze, test, and debug system performance through simulation and real-world data, conducting root-cause investigations and proposing enhancements.

• Collaborate with researchers and engineers across Perception, Prediction, and Control to ensure an integrated, reliable autonomy stack.

Qualifications

• Recently completed or soon-to-complete PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

• Research or Internship experience in one or more of the following:

• Motion planning algorithms (optimization, sampling, graph/search-based methods)

• Behavioral planning and decision-making under uncertainty

• Trajectory optimization and control

• Multi-agent interaction modeling

• Proven research ability demonstrated by publications in top-tier conferences (e.g., RSS, ICRA, IROS, CVPR, NeurIPS, CoRL).

• Hands-on experience in C++ for implementing complex, real-time algorithms.

• Excellent analytical and communication skills, with a collaborative mindset.

• For Internship Applicants: This role offers a clear pathway, with top-performing interns receiving the opportunity to convert to a full-time engineer upon successful completion of the program.
